content:
Apple shared more details about the AI labelling requirements announced for Apple Music back in March this year. Here are the specifics.

Content generated using AI will be clearly labelled on Apple Music.

Earlier this year, Apple announced that Apple Music would soon require AI transparency disclosures for cover art, songs, compositions, and music videos newly submitted to the platform.

The company has now provided further details on how this mechanism will work.

In an email sent to creators today, Apple stated: "Later this year, we will also surface these labels to Apple Music listeners in the form of a 'Made With AI' tag."

Apple has also clarified under what circumstances such disclosures must be made. The email reads as follows:

Apple Music added that the aim of this measure is "to provide as much transparency as possible to listeners," and advised creators to refer to their Music Style Guide for more information.

Apple Music's approach is just the latest example of streaming platforms responding to the influx of AI-generated music, as more and more artists incorporate generative AI into their production workflows.

Spotify recently stated that, by default, it will not include music from AI Personas in its editorial or algorithmic recommendations; Deezer also announced last year that fully AI-generated songs would be excluded from its recommendations and editorial playlists. Just last month, Deezer further reported that fully AI-generated music accounted for over 50% of daily new uploads for the first time.

On the Apple Music side, platform head Oliver Schusser revealed during a recent appearance on Billboard's "On the Record" podcast that, although more than one-third of music uploaded to Apple Music each month is fully AI-generated, it accounts for less than 0.5% of the service's total listening volume.
